findings.title: `_require_instance` is duplicated across two modules
findings.description: `_require_instance` in `instruments.py` is the same function as the one in `markets.py:136`. The only difference is the exception class raised (`InvalidInstrumentError` vs `InvalidMarketError`). The project rule says "Do not duplicate logic". `instruments.py` already imports from `markets.py`, so a shared helper would not add an import-boundary dependency. For example, a private `_validation.py` helper could take the error class as a parameter. The `_require_nonempty_str` and `_require_positive_decimal` helpers could move there too. If they stay duplicated, a fix to one copy (for example how it formats `{value!r}`) will silently miss the other.

findings.title: Unhashable inputs raise `TypeError` instead of the domain error
findings.description: `self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` and `frozenset(bases)` in `_normalize_bases` both hash their inputs. A caller who passes a list or dict for `source_bar_stamping`, or a list of lists for `adjustment_bases`, gets a raw `TypeError`. It does not get `InvalidMarketError`. The tests cover wrong-typed scalar and element values but not unhashable ones. This is low risk, since the inputs come from trusted fixtures today. It matters once markets are built from served metadata at a trust boundary.

findings.title: Fixture modules ship inside the production package
findings.description: The new `fixtures/markets.py` and `fixtures/instruments.py` follow the existing `fixtures/calendars.py` layout. They are clearly labeled "not served data" and every id has a `fixture-` prefix, so this is consistent and acceptable. Moving fixtures out of `src/` into the test tree would stop them being importable as real data.
